html:
The Austrian Netherlands were the southern Low Countries, roughly modern Belgium and Luxembourg, ruled by the Austrian Habsburgs from 1714 to 1797. They are on the map for 1715 to 1800.

Until 1714 these provinces were the Spanish Netherlands, part of the Habsburg Netherlands that stayed loyal to Spain when the Dutch Republic broke away. After the War of the Spanish Succession they passed to Austria. Dutch troops held a line of barrier forts in them as a guard against France. The emperor chartered the Ostend Company to trade with Asia, but Britain and the Dutch forced him to shut it down.

Under Maria Theresa the provinces were mostly quiet. Her son Joseph II's reforms of church and government provoked the Brabant Revolution of 1789, and the rebels briefly declared the United Belgian States. Austria returned, but revolutionary France conquered and annexed the land in 1795, and Austria gave up its claim in 1797. The region later became Belgium and Luxembourg.
sum: The Austrian Netherlands were the southern Low Countries, roughly modern Belgium and Luxembourg, ruled by the Austrian Habsburgs from 1714 to 1797. They are on the map for 1715 to 1800.
